requirements.meaning: Matter, particle models, atoms, molecules, ions, states and chemistry-facing electronic structure
requirements.evidence: Accepted C01 secures atomic/molecular/ionic identity, states of matter and electronic-structure literacy before later chemistry.

requirements.meaning: Elements, periodic organization, metals/nonmetals and foundational inorganic patterns
requirements.evidence: Accepted C02 secures periodicity, element families, metal/nonmetal meaning and inorganic/coordination foundations.

requirements.meaning: Bonding, molecular structure, intermolecular interactions and structure-property reasoning
requirements.evidence: C03 owns ionic/covalent/metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and geometry; C09 extends structure-processing-property reasoning to material classes without stealing physics ownership.

requirements.meaning: Chemical equations, atom/mass conservation, stoichiometry, reaction energy, rates and equilibrium
requirements.evidence: Accepted C04 covers equations, conservation, mole/stoichiometry, thermochemistry, kinetics and equilibrium with repaired foundational semantics.

requirements.meaning: Acid-base, oxidation-reduction, electrochemical and quantitative reaction reasoning
requirements.evidence: Accepted C04 closes acid-base, redox and electrochemistry in the reaction/equilibrium owner scope.

requirements.meaning: Mixtures, separation, qualitative/quantitative analysis, calibration, measurement evidence and analytical uncertainty
requirements.evidence: Accepted C05 covers qualitative/quantitative analysis, titration, chromatography, mass/spectral analysis and sensors with calibration/QC and evidence limits.

requirements.meaning: Carbon chemistry, functional groups, organic reactions, stereochemistry, synthesis and polymer chemistry
requirements.evidence: Accepted C06 secures carbon structure, functional groups, mechanisms, stereochemistry, synthesis and polymer chemistry before specialized medicinal/advanced extensions.

requirements.meaning: Materials, catalysts, industrial processes, green chemistry, resource use and lifecycle/sustainability reasoning
requirements.evidence: C09 covers material classes and processing-property relations; C10 covers industrial/environmental chemistry, catalysts, green chemistry, atom economy and lifecycle reasoning.

requirements.meaning: Scientific inquiry, models, measurement, evidence, assumptions, limits and increasingly formal explanation across chemistry
requirements.evidence: Across accepted child D1-D4 objectives and closures, modelling, source/evidence use, measurement, assumptions, trade-offs and model limits are explicit; C07 theoretical models and C08 biochemical chemistry extend rather than replace the foundational spine.

requirements.meaning: Coupled Earth-system, climate, global-health, food-system, policy and cultural conclusions beyond the underlying chemical mechanism or measurement
requirements.owner_scope: B1.4 and cross-domain X01/X03/X04 or other canonical branches as applicable
requirements.evidence: B1.3-C08/C10 supply chemistry-owned biomolecular, pollutant, atmospheric, water/soil and lifecycle claims. Earth-system, health, food and policy synthesis remains boundary-only and is not required to close B1.3 foundational chemistry.
